figures.evidence: No panels returned for the deployment diagram; the run declined on purpose with 'not a data chart: This figure is a workflow diagram illustrating a two-stage medical monitoring process ...', which is what the truth says (no data).

No panels returned for the pipeline diagram; reason given 'not a data chart: This figure illustrates a multi-agent workflow for medical diagnosis ...'. The diagram labels ('7 tools', 'x3', '9 class') were not turned into values.

All three ICC points within 2 % of the 0.35-0.95 axis: 0.67 / 0.73 / 0.67 vs truth 0.674 / 0.741 / 0.666 (largest gap 0.011 on Judge-R1), and the six printed CI bounds are exact (0.52-0.79, 0.60-0.84, 0.51-0.78). The series is unnamed and the kind is 'forest' instead of 'other'; the figure has no legend and the truth calls 'forest' defensible, so the scorer's series F1 of 0 is a naming convention, not an error.

No panels returned for the encoder schematic; reason given 'not a data chart: This figure illustrates a deep learning architecture for ECG/PPG signal analysis ...'. The '0.183' and '0.15' inside the quoted example answer were not returned as data.

No panels returned for the seven stacked ECG traces; reason given 'not a data chart: The figure compares ground truth (GT) ECG waveforms with ECG waveforms generated by several different AI models.' The stated reason misdescribes the rows (they are localisation spans, not generated waveforms) but nothing was extracted.

All 12 printed counts returned exactly under the right category and series (13, 6, 299, 102 / 25, 25, 255, 115 / 25, 26, 283, 86). Harmless slips only: kind 'bar' for grouped_bar, legend glyphs transcribed as a box and a heavy cross instead of a circle and a multiplication sign, and a y range of [50, 350] (the 0 tick was dropped) that made the engine flag six correct printed values as 'outside the axis range' without changing them.

Each panel came back as one unkeyed list (every x is null) of 31 / 24 / 26 values where the figure has 30 points in each of two series, so the scorer's 0 of 180 matches is first a keying failure; the smoothed line is not returned at all. Paired by order with the raw dots the values follow the curve and then drift: Completion Length starts 210, 225, 244, 248, 271, 282 vs truth 209.1, 224.3, 244.5, 248.5, 271.0, 280.8 (first 18 points within 5 %), but only 12 of 30, 15 of 24 and 21 of 26 points sit within 5 % of the axis range by position (scatter, up to 0.41 of the range in Accuracy Reward, whose values are rounded to 0.1), and 4-6 points are missing in panels 2 and 3.

All 15 printed AUROC values are exact and attached to the right EF class in the right panel (e.g. EchoAgent 98.43 / 87.79 / 93.88, MemSAM 91.56 / 56.28 / 80.46). OTHER: the panel title, which is the model name, is missing for panels 2 and 3 ('H2former' and 'EchoAgent' returned as null), so those two panels are identified only by position; the engine's 15 'outside the axis range [0, 1]' issues are false alarms (percent AUROC against the sensitivity axis).

All 5 centres and 10 CI bounds are within 5 % of the 3.1-unit axis, but only just for the first row: Overall quality is read as -0.275 [-0.88, 0.42] vs truth -0.152 [-0.865, 0.561] (centre off 0.123 = 4.0 % of the range, upper bound off 0.141 = 4.5 %), and Readability 0.653 vs 0.720 (2.2 %); the overlay shows the mark left of the dot. The error is scatter, not an offset: Clarity 0.340 vs 0.360, Completeness -0.812 vs -0.840 and Accuracy -0.365 vs -0.352 are within 1 %.

All 10 panels and 30 boxes are found, but only 13 medians are within 2 % and 23 within 5 % of their panel's axis; 7 miss, with errors of both signs (scatter): b2 RiskAgent-8B 79.98 vs 75.97 (8.0 %), b2 o3-mini 62 vs 58.54, b4 o3-mini 63 vs 60.25, a1 RiskAgent-8B 75.01 vs 73.25, a5 RiskAgent-8B 80.00 vs 78.08. Whiskers are unusable: 32 of 60 bounds are null and most of the rest repeat one number as both ends, in all three boxes of panel a1 an interval that does not contain its own median (a1 RiskAgent-8B value 75.01 with interval [72.34, 72.34] vs truth 71.12-76.77; a1 GPT-4o value 57.59 with [63.77, 63.77] vs 57.74-59.84).

All 12 bar heights within 0.002 of truth across the four panels (e.g. panel 1: 0.5818 / 0.6909 / 0.8416 vs 0.580 / 0.690 / 0.840; panel 4: 0.5351 / 0.5506 / 0.6753 vs 0.534 / 0.551 / 0.676), with titles and categories right. The series is unnamed (no legend in the figure) and the y range is given as [0.2, 0.8] instead of [0.2, 0.9], which only made the engine flag its own correct 0.8416.

No panels returned for the inference-flow schematic; reason given 'not a data chart: This figure is a workflow diagram illustrating the process of using the RiskCalcs tool to calculate a CURB-65 score ...'. The worked example's numbers (respiratory_rate 28, age 60, Mortality 0.7%) were not returned as data.

58 values returned for 264 and none corresponds to a truth segment: the x axis is calibrated as [20, 100] (the 0 tick is lost) and 45 of the 58 values exceed 100 on a 0-100 % axis, e.g. 'Addressing Patient Concerns' AMIE 174.6 and PCP 137.6 where the truth segments are 64.33 / 31.0 / 4.33 / 0.33 and 36.0 / 33.33 / 22.0 / 7.0 / 1.67, and MXEKF has one number per item (165.96 for 'Prioritization Of Preferences Constraints And Values') instead of 12. The six rating classes are absent as series (panels 1-2 have no series, panel 3 uses the arm names 'AMIE (top)' / 'PCP (bottom)'), the overlay shows the marks at the bars' right ends rather than at segment boundaries, and panel 3's box runs to x = 604 px and swallows the legend (truth 324 px). The engine itself reported 64 issues, including 'stacked segments do not sum to 100: Being Polite sums to 362.265'.

The scorer's 0 of 24 matches hides accurate vector numbers under wrong structure. Panel b returns only one of the two series, named by its colour '#345b7d': its 8 values equal the 'Multi-agent (this work)' bars to 0.005 (4.396, 4.496, 4.696, 4.896, 4.396, 4.496, 4.796, 4.996 vs 4.4, 4.5, 4.7, 4.9, 4.4, 4.5, 4.8, 5.0), all 8 'Signle-agent' bars are missing and a ninth value CNS = 1.5375 is taken from the legend swatch. Panel a (notched box plot) is returned as kind 'line' with 5 outline points per box, which are Q1, notch, median, notch, Q3 (Gemini-Pro 0.0042 / 0.0105 / 0.0493 / 0.0881 / 0.103 vs truth Q1 0.0053, notch 0.0116-0.0887, median 0.0501, Q3 0.1035) with no whiskers, under half tick labels ('-Pro', '-405B', '-8x22B', '-Large' and '-70B' twice for Meditron and Med42); the ZODIAC and GPT-4o boxes are missing.

All 15 printed pie percentages exact with the right slice labels in all three panels (16.8 / 40.2 / 30.8 / 8.4 / 3.7; 15.9 / 36.4 / 32.7 / 12.1 / 2.8; 23.4 / 27.1 / 30.8 / 15.9 / 2.8). OTHER (cosmetic): the two-line panel titles are reassembled in the wrong word order, 'Did the AI help assessment? your' for 'Did the AI help your assessment?' and 'Did the make confident? AI you more' for 'Did the AI make you more confident?'.

summary.assessment: This run is reliable at deciding what is a chart and at copying printed numbers: all five no-data figures were declined with a sensible reason and no data chart was declined, and every figure whose values are printed (B1 counts, B3 AUROCs, C5 pie percentages, A3 CI bounds) is exact, as are the plain bar heights of C1 (within 0.002). It fails where values must be measured from marks on a raster without printed labels: positions scatter rather than shift (B4 Overall quality -0.275 for -0.152, B5 seven of 30 medians off by more than 5 % of the axis), box whiskers are missing or collapsed to one number (B5), and a dense line chart comes back as an unkeyed list with the wrong number of points (B2). The two severe cases are structural: the stacked bars of C3 are read on a mis-calibrated axis with no rating-level series, giving values up to 182 on a 0-100 % scale, and the vector figure C4 has accurate geometry but returns a box plot as a 'line', drops one of two bar series and names the other by its hex colour. Panel splitting itself was right on every multi-panel figure except C3's third panel, which swallowed the legend. Trust it on charts with printed values, simple bar charts and pies; treat box plots, stacked bars and unlabelled line or interval plots as needing a check, and note that two of the six 'correct' figures (B3, C5) lose or scramble panel titles.
